pm_exper_user_1606_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I handle it in team meetings when coworkers jump in to finish my point before I’ve said it all?
pm_exper_user_1606_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) You could let your team know that it’s important for you to finish your thoughts without interruptions, since being cut off can feel frustrating. Politely saying something like, “I’d like to finish my point,” can help them give you the space you need.
(b) If coworkers tend to finish your sentences, you might explain that you work best when you can share your full idea before others respond. You could ask them to wait until you’ve paused so you can express yourself clearly without feeling rushed.
(c) If coworkers often interrupt, you could let them know that you prefer to share your whole thought before they respond. Politely signaling when you’re not done speaking can help create smoother and more respectful conversations.
(d) When someone jumps in before you finish, you could hold up your hand slightly or say, “Just a moment,” to signal you’re still speaking. This can help prevent the frustration you feel when others guess what you’re trying to say.
